{{Quote|Drop your weapons! I said drop 'em.|A security battle droid confronting Jedi intruders|<ref name="Episode III">{{Film|III}}</ref>}}
'''OOM-series security droids''', also known as '''OOM security battle droids''', were [[Security droid/Legends|security droids]] of the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] and [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] used for the purposes of defense and detection.

Security [[Droid/Legends|droids]] were characterized by red markings on their shoulders and upper abdomen, which distinguished them from other variants of the [[OOM-series battle droid/Legends|OOM model]]. They most commonly worked in [[Squad/Legends|squads]] led by an [[OOM command battle droid/Legends|OOM command battle droid]]. Trade Federation security droids fulfilling their most common role as guards on [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ships]] carried the standard weapons ([[E-5 blaster rifle/Legends|E-5 blaster rifles]]) used by similar models.

A type of [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-series battle droid]], it was used in the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation's]] [[Trade Federation Droid Army/Legends|Droid Army]], equipped with specialized programming. However, the targeting and coordination of the security droids was little better than that of their cousins, and often failed to consistently hit their target. The OOM security battle droid model saw varied use after the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].

==Characteristics==
The [[OOM-series battle droid/Legends|OOM]] [[Security droid/Legends|security]] [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droid]] were characterized by [[Color/Legends|red]] markings on their torso and shoulders. They were equipped with the [[E-5 blaster rifle/Legends|E-5 blaster rifle]] as their primary weapon. The OOM [[Security droid/Legends|security droid]] lacked in accuracy and coordination. This made it fail to consistently hit its intended target, making it easy to destroy.<ref name="tpm">{{Film|I}}</ref>

Standing 1.91 [[Meter/Legends|meters]], the security droids were produced by [[Baktoid Combat Automata/Legends|Baktoid Combat Automata]].<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Droids" />

==History==
The OOM security battle droid was manufactured by Baktoid Combat Automata as part of the OOM droid line. OOM security battle droids were created for defense and detection.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Droids" /> They generally operated in squads led by an [[OOM command battle droid/Legends|OOM command battle droids]] on [[Capital ship/Legends|Capital starships]].<ref name="tpm" /> One such group was the squad lead by [[OWO-1/Legends|OWO-1]].<ref name="tpm" />

[[File:OOM_Battle_Droids.png|thumb|left|250px|A squad of OOM security droids and the OOM [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] OWO-1]]
They were used by the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] during the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Subjugation]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]. Aboard the capital ship [[Saak'ak/Legends|''Saak'ak'']], security droids patrolled the hallways and attacked the Jedi [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]]. Security droids also accompanied [[Viceroy/Legends|Viceroy]] [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]], [[OOM-9/Legends|OOM-9]], and Queen [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Amidala]] through the streets of [[Theed/Legends|Theed]] but were then [[Capture of Theed/Legends|destroyed]].<ref name="tpm" />

OOM security droids were added to the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] when the Trade Federation committed its forces. Security droids then saw service on capital ships such as the [[Invisible Hand/Legends|Invisible Hand]].<ref name="Episode III" />

After the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] ended, many security droids were shut down. Some droids were reactivated by gangs and [[Separatist holdouts/Legends|Separatist holdouts]] serving as guards.

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Security_battle_droid.jpg|thumb|right|200px|OOM security droids, as they appear in the [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (video game)|''Revenge of the Sith'' video game]]]]
OOM security battle droids first appeared with the release of the [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']] film. The OOM designation originates with the ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'', first alluded to in the ''[[Arms & Equipment Guide]]''. There, it is described as having the same processor as the OOM Commander, as exemplified by [[OOM-9/Legends|OOM-9]] in ''The Phantom Menace'', and is first designated "OOM Series" in the "Artificial Armies" online supplement for the ''[[Star Wars Miniatures]]'' [[Clone Strike (Star Wars Miniatures)|''Clone Strike'']] expansion.

Prior to the release of [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']], security droids were claimed to have possessed intelligence and independence like the command droids, although they were still subordinate to the latter.<ref name="Star Wars: Invasion of Theed Adventure Game">[[Star Wars: Invasion of Theed Adventure Game|''Star Wars: Invasion of Theed'' Adventure Game]]</ref><ref name="Naboo">''[[Secrets of Naboo]]''</ref> Both command and security droids at the Invasion of Naboo were also described as possessing low-grade electronic brains, unlike the pilot and infantry droids.<ref name="Naboo" /> However, these claims conflict with other sources that state all those droids possessed only control signal receivers and simple processors.<ref name="Star Wars: Episode I: The Visual Dictionary">''[[Star Wars: Episode I: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref>

Security battle droids in service to the Trade Federation make an appearance in the novel ''[[Cloak of Deception]]'', but it is unclear if they are meant to be the red-marked OOM security droids or simply standard B1 battle droids without backpacks.<ref name="Cloak of Deception">''[[Cloak of Deception]]''</ref> The OOM security battle droid made a non-canonical appearance in ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Video Game]]''. They appeared on the very first level and also could be played as. In ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'', the security droids were given incorrect areas for red markings as well as having a backpack which OOM droids didn't have.
